articles.title: An ancient failed rift is reawakening inside one of Africa's oldest landmasses
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: In April 2017, a magnitude 6.5 earthquake shook southern Africa from an unlikely place: the middle of the Kalahari Craton in eastern Botswana. Cratons are the ancient cores of continents, and this one is built from blocks of crust up to 3.7 billion years old. Geologists have long considered such regions too cold, too thick and too rigid to tear apart.

articles.title: Fermi's 14-year all-sky map bridges astronomy's elusive 'MeV gap'
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Gamma rays, the most high-energy type of electromagnetic radiation in the universe, have always had a blind spot. We've always had trouble measuring them in the "megaelectronvolt" (MeV) energy range, which astronomers have taken to calling the "MeV gap." But a new paper from an international group of scientists working with the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) Collaboration, recently published in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, takes a stab at closing that gap by identifying 450 cosmic sources in the 20–200 MeV range, providing the clearest view of low-energy gamma rays ever.
